title: Equality Before Law
content: Article 14 guarantees that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. It prohibits arbitrary state action and forms the bedrock of natural justice and non-discrimination.
precedents: E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu (AIR 1974 SC 555)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (AIR 1978 SC 597)

title: Protection of Certain Rights Regarding Freedom of Speech, etc.
content: Article 19 guarantees fundamental freedoms: 19(1)(a) Freedom of speech and expression; 19(1)(b) Peaceful assembly without arms; 19(1)(c) Form associations/unions; 19(1)(d) Move freely throughout India; 19(1)(e) Reside and settle in any part of India; 19(1)(g) Practice any profession, trade or business. Subject to reasonable restrictions under Art 19(2)-(6) such as sovereignty, security, public order, and morality.
precedents: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) 5 SCC 1
Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras (1950)

title: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty
content: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Encompasses right to privacy, right to clean environment, right to free legal aid, right to speedy trial, right against custodial torture, and right to live with dignity.
precedents: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) 10 SCC 1
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
Hussainara Khatoon v. Home Secretary, Bihar (1979)

title: Protection Against Arrest and Detention in Certain Cases
content: Guarantees rights of an arrested person: Right to be informed of grounds of arrest as soon as may be, right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice, and mandatory production before nearest Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest excluding transit time.
precedents: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (AIR 1997 SC 610)

title: Remedies for Enforcement of Fundamental Rights (Writ Jurisdiction)
content: Article 32 confers right to move the Supreme Court, and Article 226 confers power on High Courts, to issue writs of Habeas Corpus (release illegal detainee), Mandamus (command public duty), Prohibition, Quo Warranto (challenge office title), and Certiorari (quash illegal judicial order).
precedents: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997)

title: Punishment for Murder and Mob Lynching
content: Section 103(1) prescribes death penalty or imprisonment for life, and fine, for committing murder. Section 103(2) specifically penalizes mob lynching where a group of 5 or more persons acting in concert commits murder on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, or personal belief, punishable with death or life imprisonment.
precedents: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) Rarest of Rare doctrine
Tehseen S. Poonawalla v. Union of India (2018)

title: Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder & Rash Driving Death
content: Section 105 penalizes culpable homicide not amounting to murder with imprisonment up to life or 10 years and fine. Section 106 penalizes causing death by negligence (rash driving/negligence) with up to 5 years imprisonment; if offender escapes scene without reporting to police/magistrate (hit and run), imprisonment extends up to 10 years and fine.

title: Theft, Cheating and Dishonest Inducement of Property
content: Section 303 defines theft (movable property taken dishonestly without consent) punishable up to 3 years imprisonment. Section 318 (IPC 420 equivalent) penalizes cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

title: Criminal Trespass, House Trespass and Forgery
content: Section 329 penalizes entering into or upon property in possession of another with intent to commit offence or intimidate. Section 334 penalizes forgery of documents, valuable security, or electronic record with intent to support claim or cause damage.

title: Sexual Offences & Cruelty by Husband or Relatives
content: Section 63 defines rape and sexual assault with rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years up to life. Section 85 (IPC 498A equivalent) penalizes husband or relative subjecting woman to cruelty (mental or physical harassment for dowry/demands) with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine.
precedents: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273
Social Action Forum for Manav Adhikar v. UOI (2018)

title: Arrest Procedure & Zero FIR / Electronic FIR Ingestion
content: Section 35 mandates notice of appearance prior to arrest for offences punishable under 7 years (Arnesh Kumar rule). Section 173 mandates registration of Information regarding cognizable offences (FIR), permitting Zero FIR (any police station irrespective of jurisdiction) and e-FIR (electronic communication recorded within 3 days).
precedents: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P. (2014) 2 SCC 1

title: Bail for Undertrials, Non-Bailable Offences & Anticipatory Bail
content: Section 479 mandates maximum period for undertrial detention (release on bail if served 1/3rd of max period for first time offenders or 1/2 for others). Section 480 governs bail conditions for non-bailable offences by Sessions/Magistrate. Section 482 (CrPC 438 equivalent) grants power to High Court/Sessions Court to grant Anticipatory Bail to person apprehending arrest.
precedents: Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI (2022) 10 SCC 51
Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab (1980)

title: Admissibility of Electronic Records & Hash Key Verification
content: Section 61 affirms that electronic records shall have same legal effect as paper documents. Section 63 (Evidence Act 65B equivalent) prescribes conditions for admissibility of electronic records (CCTV, WhatsApp, emails, server logs) requiring certificate signed by person in charge verifying computer operational status and hash integrity.
precedents: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer (2014) 10 SCC 473
Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao (2020)

title: Temporary Injunctions, Status Quo & Rejection of Plaint
content: Order 39 Rules 1 & 2 empower Civil Courts to grant temporary injunctions or status quo orders to prevent alienation/destruction of property during trial. Order 7 Rule 11 mandates rejection of plaint where it does not disclose cause of action or is barred by law.
precedents: Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v. Kartick Das (1994)
Dahiben v. Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali (2020)

title: Essential Elements of Valid Contract, Restraint of Trade & Breach Damages
content: Section 10 requires free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and lawful object for a valid contract. Section 27 voids agreements in restraint of trade/profession. Section 73 entitles non-defaulting party to compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract naturally arising in usual course of things.
precedents: Hadley v. Baxendale (1854)
Percept D'Mark v. Zaheer Khan (2006)

title: Dishonour of Cheque for Insufficiency of Funds & Director Liability
content: Section 138 penalizes cheque bounce due to insufficient funds with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to double cheque amount. Pre-requisites: Presentment within 3 months, legal demand notice within 30 days of memo, 15 days payment window. Section 141 holds directors/officers in charge of company business vicariously liable.
precedents: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra (2014)
SMS Pharmaceuticals v. Neeta Bhalla (2005)

title: Consumer Rights, District Commission Jurisdiction & Product Liability
content: Section 2(7) defines consumer including offline and e-commerce buyers. Section 35 provides for filing consumer complaint before District Commission for defective goods, deficient service, or unfair trade practice. Section 84 enforces strict product liability against manufacturer/seller for manufacturing defect or inadequate warning.

act_or_court_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
title: Application to Magistrate, Protection Orders & Shared Household Rights
content: Section 12 allows aggrieved woman or Protection Officer to apply to Magistrate for relief. Section 18 empowers Magistrate to issue Protection Orders prohibiting abettors from committing domestic violence, entering place of employment, or contacting victim. Section 19 secures right to reside in shared household regardless of legal title.
precedents: Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja (2020) 10 SCC 637
Rajnesh v. Neha (2021) 2 SCC 324

title: Offence of Money Laundering, Punishment & Twin Conditions for Bail
content: Section 3 defines money laundering as directly/indirectly indulging or assisting in process/activity connected with proceeds of crime. Section 4 penalizes with rigorous imprisonment 3 to 7 years (up to 10 years for NDPS scheduled offences). Section 45 imposes strict twin conditions for bail: Public Prosecutor opportunity to oppose and Court satisfaction that accused is not guilty.
precedents: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India (2022) SCC OnLine SC 929
Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement (2024)

section_or_case_ref: Section 66C, Section 66D IT Act & DPDP Act 2023
title: Identity Theft, Cyber Phishing & Digital Data Protection
content: Section 66C penalizes identity theft (fraudulent use of electronic signature/password/OTP) with up to 3 years imprisonment. Section 66D penalizes cheating by personation using computer resource. Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 regulates processing of digital personal data, mandating explicit consent and penalty up to Rs 250 Crore for data breaches.

title: Return of Amount and Compensation for Delayed Flat Possession
content: Section 18 mandates that if promoter fails to complete or give possession of apartment/flat in accordance with agreement for sale date, promoter is liable to return amount received with interest at prescribed rate and compensation if homebuyer wishes to withdraw. If homebuyer does not withdraw, promoter must pay monthly interest delay compensation.
precedents: Imperia Structures Ltd. v. Anil Patni (2020) 10 SCC 783
Newtech Promoters v. State of UP (2021)

title: Request for Obtaining Information & Exemption from Disclosure
content: Section 6 allows any citizen to submit RTI application in English/Hindi/official language specifying information sought. Public Information Officer (PIO) must respond within 30 days (48 hours if life/liberty involved). Section 8 lists exemptions (security of state, cabinet papers, trade secrets, fiduciary relationship unless larger public interest warrants).
precedents: Central Public Information Officer, SC v. Subhash Chandra Agarwal (2020) 5 SCC 1

title: Divorce on Contested Grounds & Divorce by Mutual Consent
content: Section 13 specifies contested divorce grounds: Cruelty, Desertion for 2+ years, Adultery, Conversion, Insanity. Section 13B provides for Divorce by Mutual Consent where spouses have lived separately for 1 year or more and mutually agree to dissolve marriage. Supreme Court under Art 142 can waive 6-month statutory waiting cooling period if marriage is irretrievably broken down.
precedents: Shilpa Sailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan (2023) 6 SCC 402
Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8 SCC 746

title: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) & Moratorium
content: Section 7 allows Financial Creditor and Section 9 allows Operational Creditor to initiate CIRP before NCLT on default of threshold amount. Section 14 mandates declaration of Moratorium prohibiting institution/continuation of suits, execution of decrees, or transfer of corporate debtor assets during insolvency resolution.
precedents: Swiss Ribbons Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India (2019) 4 SCC 17
Innova Home v. Kotak (2018)
